m40: 💡 Keeps 4 days chilled or freeze chicken and potatoes together for 2 months; reheat at 60–70% microwave power with a splash of water so the breast stays juicy rather than rubbery.
💡 Pull the breasts at 74°C on a probe rather than cooking to time; keep the green beans in a separate pot and add them cold to avoid grey, mushy beans.
m37: 💡 Cod dries out fast, so eat within 3 days and skip the freezer once cooked; reheat gently at 50% microwave power for 90 seconds, covered, or eat the flaked fish cold.
💡 Pat the fillets dry and add them to the tray only after the potatoes have had their 25 minutes, otherwise the fish overcooks while the potatoes are still firm.
m04: 💡 Keeps 5 days refrigerated and freezes well for 3 months; reheat from chilled at full power for 3 minutes, stirring the mince halfway so it heats evenly.
💡 Cut white and sweet potato into cubes of the same size and spread them in a single layer; crowded trays steam rather than roast and you lose the crisp edges.
m21: 💡 Store nuggets 4 days chilled or freeze on a tray before bagging; reheat in the air fryer at 190°C for 5–6 minutes, never the microwave, or the cornflake crust goes soft.
💡 Press the crushed cornflakes firmly onto each ball and leave space between them in the basket so the coating dries out and crisps rather than steaming.
m43: 💡 The frittata keeps 4 days chilled and freezes in individual wedges for a month; reheat at 50% microwave power for 2 minutes so the egg whites do not turn spongy.
💡 Squeeze excess liquid from the wilted spinach before pouring in the eggs, otherwise water pools under the frittata and the base never sets properly.
m46: 💡 Best eaten cold within 4 days; do not freeze, as the cucumber and tomato turn watery. If you want it warm, reheat only the chicken and put it back over the cold salad.
💡 Rinse the drained orzo briefly under cold water and toss it with lemon juice while still warm, which stops it clumping into one solid block in the container.
v4: 💡 Eat within 3 days and do not freeze, as scrambled egg and cottage cheese both weep liquid when thawed; reheat at 50% power for 90 seconds or eat the egg layer cold.
💡 Pull the eggs off the heat while still glossy and stir the cottage cheese in off the heat, otherwise reheating later tips them from soft curds into rubber.
hol3: 💡 Sliced lamb keeps 4 days and freezes for 2 months without the sauce; reheat lamb and quinoa at 60% power for 2 minutes, then add the mint yogurt cold from a separate pot.
💡 Rest the lamb the full 10 minutes before slicing thinly across the grain; carving straight from the oven pushes the juices out onto the board.
m53: 💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 2 months minus the cherry tomatoes; reheat in the air fryer at 180°C for 4 minutes to bring the sweet potato edges back.
💡 Air fry the sweet potato in a single layer and shake the basket at 12 minutes; a heaped basket gives you soft steamed cubes instead of golden ones.
m57: 💡 Keeps 4 days chilled; freeze the chicken and sweet potato only, since spinach and cottage cheese turn watery. Keep the cottage cheese in a separate pot and add it after reheating.
💡 Toss the spinach in for the final 2 minutes only, as written; any longer in the air fryer and it turns to brittle flakes that blow around the basket.
m59: 💡 Beef and sweet potato keep 5 days and freeze for 3 months; portion the cottage cheese, tomatoes and red onion into a separate pot so they stay cold while you microwave the base.
💡 Drain the mince in a sieve for a full minute after browning; pooled fat left in the container sets into white flecks and makes the sweet potato greasy.
m62: 💡 Eat within 3 days and do not freeze; the avocado and cucumber are best cold, so reheat only the salmon at 50% power for 60 seconds if you want it warm.
💡 Toss the avocado pieces in the lemon juice before sealing and press cling film directly onto them in the container, which slows browning far better than a lid alone.
m25: 💡 Mac and chicken keep 4 days in separate containers; freeze the mac for up to 2 months, but the coated chicken loses its crust after thawing, so eat that fresh.
💡 Keep the sauce on the lowest heat and add the cheddar off the boil; evaporated milk splits and goes grainy if it simmers hard once the cheese is in.
hol8: 💡 Keeps 3 days chilled and should not be frozen because the strawberries collapse; add the almonds and yogurt dressing from a separate pot just before eating so they stay crunchy and cold.
💡 Line the tray with baking paper because the honey glaze caramelises and welds to bare metal; cool the quinoa fully before folding in spinach or it wilts to sludge.
m20: 💡 Sliced chicken keeps 4 days and freezes for 3 months; reheat at 60% microwave power in 60-second bursts, or add it cold to salads and wraps.
💡 Wipe most of the yogurt marinade off before air frying; a thick coating stays pale and pasty, while a thin film chars nicely in 30 minutes at 180°C.
v1: 💡 Dahl keeps 5 days and freezes for 3 months without the yogurt and cottage cheese; reheat from chilled with 50 ml water at full power, stirring twice, and add the dairy afterwards.
💡 Stir from the bottom every 5–10 minutes during the simmer; red lentils catch and scorch on the base of the pot once the mixture starts to thicken.
hol1: 💡 Turkey breast keeps 4 days and freezes for 3 months; reheat at 60% microwave power with a teaspoon of water, then spoon the Greek yogurt and cranberry sauce on from a separate pot.
💡 Turkey breast has almost no fat to protect it, so probe from 35 minutes and pull at 74°C; every extra 5 minutes past that turns the slices dry and stringy.
hol7: 💡 Eat within 3 days; salmon portioned with yogurt sauce does not freeze well. Reheat quinoa and salmon at 50% power for 90 seconds and add the caper yogurt cold.
💡 Thick asparagus needs the full 18 minutes but thin spears are done in 10, so add pencil-thin spears to the tray halfway through the salmon roast.
m19: 💡 This burrito is made to be eaten within the hour; chill the salmon-avocado filling for up to 2 days and roll and crisp the wrap fresh, since a stored wrap goes leathery.
💡 Drain excess yogurt sauce off the filling before rolling and tuck the ends in tightly; a wet filling soaks through the wrap and it splits in the air fryer.
m34: 💡 Keeps 3 days refrigerated; salmon reheats best at 50% microwave power for 60–90 seconds under a damp paper towel, or flake it cold through the quinoa as a salad.
💡 Roast skin-side down on the lined sheet; the skin shields the flesh from the tray heat and peels away cleanly once the fish has cooled, leaving neat fillets for portioning.
m27: 💡 Keeps 4 days chilled; freeze individual slices wrapped tightly for a month and reheat at 50% power for 2–3 minutes so the eggs warm through without splitting.
💡 Salt the zucchini slices and blot them for 10 minutes before layering, otherwise their water floods the smashed sweet potato base and the eggs set in a puddle.
m36: 💡 Keeps 3 days refrigerated with the dressing on, or 4 if dressed on the day; never freeze, as the cucumber turns to water and the chickpeas go mealy.
💡 Slice the red onion paper-thin and soak it in the lemon juice for 10 minutes before mixing, which softens the raw bite that otherwise dominates by day two.
v9: 💡 Slices keep 4 days in the fridge and freeze for a month between sheets of baking paper; reheat at 60% microwave power for 90 seconds or eat cold on the go.
💡 Steam the broccoli and sauté the capsicum first as written; raw vegetables release water during the bake and leave a soggy layer at the bottom of the dish.
bf4: 💡 Season the cottage cheese for the week and keep it in a sealed tub for 4 days; toast and assemble each morning, since dressed toast goes soft within 20 minutes.
💡 Drain any whey off the top of the tub and sit the sliced cucumber and tomato on kitchen paper first, otherwise the toast turns wet before you finish it.
bf8: 💡 Portion the yogurt into pots for 4 days but add the seeds on the day so they stay crunchy; frozen berries thaw into the yogurt overnight and make a natural swirl.
💡 If adding protein powder, whisk it into a spoonful of yogurt to make a paste first, then fold in the rest; tipping it straight in leaves dry lumps.
bf10: 💡 Make up to 3 jars ahead; the oats thicken overnight, so loosen with a splash of milk in the morning. Add banana and peanut butter on the day, as the banana browns.
💡 Dissolve the whey in the milk before adding oats and yogurt, otherwise the powder clumps into chalky pockets that you find at the bottom of the jar.
bf11: 💡 Blend and eat straight away, since the bowl softens to a drink within 15 minutes; if you must make it ahead, freeze the blended base in a pot and stir it after 10 minutes on the bench.
💡 Load the almond milk and yogurt into the blender first, then powder, then frozen berries on top, and pulse rather than run it flat out to keep the mix thick.
bf13: 💡 Jars keep 3 days in the fridge; the oats absorb the milk overnight, so loosen with a splash of skimmed milk. The chocolate whey and cinnamon deepen after a night chilled.
💡 Stir the whey into the yogurt and milk until glossy before the oats go in; add blueberries last and fold gently so they do not bleed purple through the whole jar.
bf14: 💡 Make 3 jars at a time and add the banana on the morning you eat it; sliced banana left in the jar browns and goes slimy by the second day.
💡 If the mixture is stiff after a night in the fridge, add 20 ml skimmed milk rather than water, which thins it without diluting the chocolate whey flavour.
bf15: 💡 Prep the oat base for 3 days but melt the chocolate and add banana and biscuit the morning you eat it; a stored drizzle sets hard and the biscuit goes soft.
💡 Melt the 15 g of dark chocolate in 20-second bursts at 50% power; it looks solid until stirred, and one extra burst at full power seizes it into a grainy lump.
d5: 💡 Cool the tray completely, ideally 2 hours or overnight in the fridge, before slicing; warm banana brownies tear, and the squares firm up noticeably once chilled.
💡 Freeze squares on a tray, then bag them for 2 months; thaw in the fridge overnight or microwave from frozen for 20 seconds for a warm, fudgy portion.
ds2: 💡 These are meant to live in the freezer; keep them in a sealed tub with baking paper between layers and eat straight from frozen, as a thawed rice cake goes soft and chewy within 10 minutes.
💡 Spread the yogurt layer right to the edge and get the melted chocolate over it quickly to seal the surface, or the rice cake underneath draws in moisture and loses its snap.
d4: 💡 Bake the loaf up to 5 days ahead but store it untopped in the fridge and add the matcha yogurt and berries per slice, since a topped loaf weeps within a day.
💡 Blend the cottage cheese until no curds remain and test the centre with a skewer at 30 minutes; protein powder loaves look done on top while still wet in the middle.
d1: 💡 Unfrosted cookies keep 5 days in the fridge and freeze for 2 months; frost only the ones you plan to eat that day, as the yogurt frosting softens the cookie beneath.
💡 Add the almond milk a tablespoon at a time and wait a minute between additions; coconut flour keeps absorbing liquid, so a dough that looks dry often needs less than you think.
pw2: 💡 Peel and freeze the bananas in halves rather than whole; halves blend without straining the motor, and bagging oats and powder per serving gets you a one-minute morning.
💡 Blend the almond milk with the oats first for 20 seconds, then add banana and powder; this softens the oats so the smoothie is smooth rather than gritty and stays drinkable.
pw6: 💡 Decant the chocolate milk into 250 ml bottles for the week and keep the bananas out of the fridge; a cold banana goes grey and mealy while a room-temperature one ripens on schedule.
💡 Have this 30–45 minutes before training as written; if you are prone to a sloshing stomach, halve the milk, keep the rice cakes, and drink the rest after the session.
